owned_question: Under what algebraic laws (associativity, commutativity where declared, idempotency, identity/annihilator elements) do transformations and operators compose in a semantic library, such that Merge, Join, Satisfy, pipeline composition, lineage edges, and distributed dataflow operators remain observable, provable, and correctly attributed — including what residual (unabsorbed difference) each composite operation leaves behind?
terms: typed pipeline and natural constraint on composition
non_collapse_laws: operator association order is observable through intermediate-state carriers (e.g. partition-level intermediate artifacts), never hidden by the composer
merging two composites must not silently absorb their provenance differences; the residual between naive-merged and structurally-composed results is a first-class artifact

an operator's declared idempotency must be evidenced against a specific carrier equality, not assumed globally — duplicate-attribution checks fail loudly when the carrier equality is weaker than the operator's equality
join operators must carry and expose their join keys as part of composed type information; key-blindness is not collapse but refusal-with-residual
replacing a composite pipeline by an 'equivalent' fused operator requires an explicit proof obligation against the algebra's laws, not an internal rewrite invisible to lineage consumers
Satisfy-type constraint conjunction composes monotonically: conjoining contracts may only narrow accepted behavior, and every narrowing that rejects a previously-passing input is recorded as residual
failure/complement of one operator in a distributed DAG is observable and recoverable via lineage replay, never conflated with success of another
carrier_requirements: a deterministic intermediate-state artifact per composition step (RDD-style lineage-partitioned record) sufficient for replay and diffing
explicit join-key signature attached to any Join/composite so attribution duplicates are detectable
a law-manifest per operator: declared associativity, identity, idempotency, and the equality relation on which they were checked
residual carriers: explicit representation of merged-minus-inputs and inputs-minus-merged (unsatisfied contract remainder)
typed edge labels for lineage edges binding producer output type to consumer input type
operations_or_relations: compose (sequential operator chaining under typed interfaces)
merge (union of datasets/effects with declared idempotency or else visible residual)
join (keyed relational join with join-key exposure)
residual_merge (merge returning both result and per-input unsatisfied remainder)
replay (recover a state by re-executing its lineage edge set)
fusion_proof_obligation (optimize-by-fusing only against a discharged law proof)
invariants: replay determinism: re-executing the same lineage graph over the same inputs yields byte-equal outputs (Spark RDD §5 design point)
attribution uniqueness: every output row/element maps to exactly one non-duplicated derivation path given exposed join keys
monotonicity of satisfy: adding constraints never increases accepted behavior
identity preservation: composing with the declared unit leaves both value and lineage unchanged
association observability: (f ∘ g) ∘ h vs f ∘ (g ∘ h) differ only where the algebra's law manifest licenses it; intermediate carriers exist for either bracketing
refusals: refuse to treat associativity as automatic — accept only operators whose law manifest declares it and names its evidence
refuse joins without declared keys rather than guessing keys and duplicating attribution
refuse silent deduplication: idempotent merge collapses duplicates only under the manifest-stated equality; otherwise emit residual
refuse vendor-defined optimization passes (e.g. undocumented query rewrites) as authority for equivalence without a checkable law discharge
refuse composition across unlabelled lineage edges (type gap) even if values would happen to fit
counterexamples: join-key blindness: fusing a Join while discarding key metadata produces duplicate attribution when a fact row matches multiple dimension rows under a coarser equality than intended — falsifies any claim that merge idempotency holds globally

non-deterministic downstream operator breaking replay: if one vertex's execution depends on scheduling order, recomputation from lineage yields different bytes, falsifying 'determinism by replay' unless the algebra restricts vertices to deterministic functions
constraint-conjunction fallacy: two individually-Satisfied partial proofs whose conjunction fails on shared hidden assumptions — falsifies treating Satisfy as closed under arbitrary pairing

unlawful fusion: replacing map(f)∘map(g) by map(f then g) is lawful, but the same rewrite applied to a stateful aggregator changes results, proving fusion proofs cannot be carried over by analogy between operator classes
authority_limit: Primary literature constrains the abstract algebra (program algebra laws, relational operator semantics, lineage-based recovery, typed functorial pipelines) but does NOT prescribe any concrete schema for residuals, contract-conjunction syntax, or this compiler's Join metadata format; those are lane-local designs that must cite these works only for the mathematical and systems-theoretic properties stated, not for API choices.

sources.title: Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing
sources.authors_or_issuer: Matei Zaharia, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Tathagata Das, Ankur Dave, Justin Ma, Murphy McCauley, Michael J. Franklin, Scott Shenker, Ion Stoica (UC Berkeley); USENIX NSDI '12
sources.source_class: peer-reviewed original paper (Best Paper Award), open access
bounded_claims_supported: lineage graphs over deterministic coarse-grained transformations support deterministic replay and fault recovery
fine-grained (per-record) updates degrade lineage reconstruction, bounding what compose/replay can promise
operator granularity choice is a semantic decision affecting recovery costs
claims_not_supported: any notion of contract residuals or Satisfy conjunction
idempotency laws for general merge outside its Transformation/Dataset abstractions
sources.limitations: cluster-data system context; its determinism argument presupposes deterministic narrow/wide dependency classification, which must be re-derived, not imported wholesale.

sources.title: Foundations of Databases: The Logical Level
sources.authors_or_issuer: Serge Abiteboul, Richard Hull, Victor Vianu; Addison-Wesley / webdam INRIA open full text
sources.edition_or_version: 1995 edition, full-text PDFs posted by authors
bounded_claims_supported: algebraic characterization of relational operators: selection, projection, join, union, difference as a calculus with known identities and containment results
conjunctive-query containment and its connection to homomorphisms (basis for what 'equivalent composition' means for Satisfy-like conjunctive fragments)
semantics of set-vs-bag distinction relevant to idempotent merge
claims_not_supported: any probabilistic or approximate merge semantics
sources.limitations: finite flat-relation setting; no lineage carriers and no streaming/operator-graph runtime semantics; equational results must be lifted case-by-case.

sources.title: Dryad: Distributed Data-Parallel Programs from Sequential Building Blocks
sources.authors_or_issuer: Michael Isard, Mihai Budiu, Yuan Yu, Andrew Birrell, Dennis Fetterly (Microsoft Research Silicon Valley); EuroSys 2007 / ACM
sources.source_class: peer-reviewed original paper (free author copy via Microsoft Research)
bounded_claims_supported: composition model where applications combine computational vertices and communication channels into a DAG with the engine handling concurrency
encoding of structured operations (including relational-style join and merge) as subgraphs — precedent for operator → algebra-of-DAG reduction
edge/channel abstraction as the typed lineage-edge analogue
claims_not_supported: equational laws among vertices (Dryad does not prove associativity/idempotency; it provides mechanism, not algebra)
sources.limitations: pre-RDD system; publisher is also a vendor, though the cited object is peer-reviewed academic work rather than a product document; lineage story is weaker than RDDs.

sources.title: The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Lambdacorrectness
sources.authors_or_issuer: Tyler Akidau, Alex Balikov, Kaya Bekiroğlu, Slava Chernyak, Josh Haberman, Reuven Lax, Sam McVeety, Daniel Mills, Paul Nordstrom, Ross Whizginsky, Sasha Zubtsov (Google); PVLDB Vol. 8 No. 12
bounded_claims_supported: correctness-equivalent composition windows/triggers/watermarks as composable semantic axes for unbounded data
exactly-once vs at-least-once accumulation modes as an explicit, user-visible composition property (directly bearing on idempotent merge semantics)
proving that streaming composition choices are observables, not implementation details
claims_not_supported: anything about cost models or any particular commercial product's guarantees
sources.limitations: streaming/unbounded-data framing; accumulation-mode and windowing idioms require translation before reuse as generic merge laws.

sources.title: Monads for Functional Programming
sources.authors_or_issuer: Philip Wadler (University of Glasgow); Marktoberdorf Summer School proceedings, Springer
sources.edition_or_version: author preprint of the published chapter
bounded_claims_supported: monadic composition as the canonical typed-pipeline discipline (compose/bind with unit; associativity as observable law)
skipping-vs-propagating evaluator pairs showing how failures thread through composition with the laws held fixed
category-theory-free practical presentation: laws stated by equational examples rather than category formalism
claims_not_supported: distributed execution, lineage, or partitioned carriers
any claim that all domain effects form a monad — evidence must be checked per effect signature
sources.limitations: single-thread functional-programming scope; no data-parallel or provenance content.

sources.title: Algebra of Programming
sources.authors_or_issuer: Richard Bird, Oege de Moor; Prentice Hall International Series in Computer Science
sources.source_class: original monograph (print); official publisher-side university page verified
bounded_claims_supported: existence of a program-level calculus (relational algebra of programs, folds/unfolds, hylomorphisms, greedy/dynamic-programming derivations) in which compositional rewrites are law-governed — the deepest precedent for fusion_proof_obligation
only supplementary materials (bibliography, programs, solutions) are openly downloadable from the cited page
claims_not_supported: specific lemma numbers or theorem statements cited from the body text (full text not openly accessible; cannot quote-checked here)
sources.limitations: full text out of print / print-only; page confirms availability status only. Treat any detailed reliance on its internal theory as a vacancy until the text is obtained.

evidence_vacancies_if_any: Bird & de Moor Algebra of Programming: no authoritative open full text; the precise fold-unfold/fusion lemmas wanted for operator refactoring laws are inaccessible for direct quotation (URI above verifies existence, not content)

no primary source found covering contract composition residuals as a formal notion (design-by-contract refinement calculi would be candidates; none was verifiable as open-access primary literature within this pass)

bag-semantics equational laws for modern engines (beyond set-based Foundations of Databases treatment) lack a canonical primary reference; needs a dedicated search for peer-reviewed bag-algebra papers
